mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between GDPC1 YoY decline > 2% and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: Joint occurrence of GDPC1 and HOUST double-digit declines is not followed by a statistically significant negative S&P 500 20-day return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% month-on-month, combined with a federal funds rate below 2%, signals inflationary pressure with accommodative policy, which initially boosts risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.5 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), following three months of consecutive declines, signals a reversal in labor market conditions and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp after 3 months of consecutive declines
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between UNRATE reversal and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes across all regimes.
